note: Hebrew migrash is open grazing land around a town (v.3: "for their cattle"); "suburbs" now suggests residential districts (also vv.3-7).

mine: with a stone in the hand
note: Hebrew be'even yad is "a hand-stone", a stone held or wielded in the hand (parallel to the wooden "hand" object in v.18), not specifically a thrown one.
Hebrew kofer is a ransom or payment in exchange for a life; "satisfaction" in this sense is obsolete outside theology (also v.32).
